shareValue: A metric-selection test for products designed to finish a task quickly.
caption:
Built an app whose entire job is to get out of your way. Side effect: the only way to confirm it works is to physically do it on a real phone.

Six years in, still no way around that.

slides.text: The best session in this app lasts five seconds.
WhatsApp won't let you message a number you haven't saved.
slides.kicker: So every one-time conversation costs you a permanent contact.

slides.text: My address book became a graveyard of people I messaged once.

slides.kicker: It builds a link and passes you to the real messaging app. The app itself does not transmit your message.

slides.text: Which means I can't test it on my computer.
slides.kicker: The Simulator has no WhatsApp. No Telegram. No Line. The one thing this app exists to do only works on a real phone.

slides.text: Choose a metric that matches the job
items: What result matters after they leave?

captions.instagram:
The best session in this app lasts five seconds.

Enter a number. Choose the messaging app. Land in the conversation. InstantMessage succeeds by sending you somewhere else as quickly as possible.

That makes engagement a terrible success metric here. Time saved and tasks completed matter more than minutes spent inside the product. Share the last slide with a team choosing its success metric.

Which popular metric would mislead your product?
